title: SessionWaitParams
description: Params of the session.wait agent tool (ADR-0020 decision 2's renewable clause, nocx-6dzxq): answer nocx about a command you started that is still running and has gone quiet. It never starts anything and it never re-runs the command — `continue` re-attaches to the SAME execution, which has been running the whole time. Reach for it only with a run id nocx handed you in a 'STILL RUNNING' result. It is a separate tool from session.run because it carries no command: the effect of a command is decided from its text, and a continuation has none to decide from. The model is untrusted input and gets the same check the renderer's parameters get — additionalProperties: false plus an explicit required list.

runId.description: The run nocx asked you about, exactly as it named it. It identifies one execution, not a session and not a command, so an answer can never land on a different command running in the same place.

decision.description: `continue` keeps waiting on that same execution — it is not restarted and nothing is re-run. `stop` ends it: the process group is signalled and the run reports that you stopped it. There is no third answer; a command nobody is waiting on is what this question exists to prevent.

quietSeconds.description: Optional, and only meaningful with `continue`. How long the command may print nothing before you are asked again. You can only ask for LESS than the person's limit; a larger number is cut down and the result says so. It cannot extend the person's overall limit on the command, which keeps running from when the command started.

result.title: SessionWaitResult
result.description: What session.wait hands back when the command it was waiting on FINALLY ENDS: the same shape session.run returns, deliberately — there is one answer for 'this command finished', and a second one would be a second thing to learn. If the command is still quiet when the new bound is reached you get another 'STILL RUNNING' message instead of this, and may answer again. `stop` never produces this shape at all: it produces a message saying the command was ended, so a stopped command can never read as one that returned nothing.

sessionId.description: The session the command ran in.

entryId.description: The ledger entry the command was recorded as. Empty when the store wrote no row (history off), which is an honest answer and not an error.

exitCode.description: The process exit status, or null when the block has none.

stopped.description: True only when the person stopped this command.

message.description: Directive shown to the model when the person stopped the command.

total.description: Total lines of output the block holds.

window.description: The span asked for: the whole output.

returned.description: The span actually returned. Narrower than `window` when the output was clamped.

truncated.description: True when the returned text was shortened by the declaration's byte bound.

dropped.description: Output bytes omitted from the returned text.

remaining.description: Output bytes still omitted from this response.

text.description: The output itself, over the returned span.

quietSeconds.description: The silence bound this continuation was held to. 0 means none was armed.

wallClockSeconds.description: The person's ceiling for the command, counted from when it started. Unchanged by any continuation.

clamped.description: True when this call asked for a longer silence bound than the person allows and was cut down to `quietSeconds`.

askedSeconds.description: What this call asked for, present only when it was clamped.

bounds.description: The two bounds this execution ran under.

message.const: The person stopped this command. Do not retry it.
